data.name: Kameshwari
data.gender_notes: Kameshwari is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Goddess of Desire and Pleasure. Kame means desire and Shwari means the fulfiller. Worshipped as the goddess of love and fertility. The name Kameshwari carries the meaning “Goddess of Desire” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kameshwari usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of desire and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of love, desire, and fulfillment.
data.etymology: Kameshwari belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Desire.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kameshwari total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The Hindu goddess Kameshwari embodies the aspects of desire, attraction, love, and pleasure. She is widely worshipped, particularly in South India, as the giver of all earthly pleasures and material desires. Her festivals and rituals are celebrated with great joy and devotion, symbolizing the human quest for happiness and fulfillment.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Goddess Kameshwari represents the innate human need for desire and pleasure, which are integral parts of our existence as emotions that help us connect with the divine and experience bliss and joy. She encourages us to seek and fulfill our deepest desires in a way that brings us closer to our ultimate spiritual goal. Ultimately, the goddess releases us from the bondage of desire and material attachment, leading us towards enlightenment and divine union.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kameshwari symbolizes the embodiment of desire and passion, representing the goddess of fulfillment and satisfaction in material and spiritual aspects of life. She is the Goddess of love, desire, and sex, who grants the deepest longings and cherished wishes.

historical_references.reference: The Goddess Kameshwari is mentioned in the ancient Hindu scripture, the Shiva Purana. In this text, she is described as the consort of Lord Shiva and the goddess of desire. She is also known as the goddess of love, fertility, and pleasure.

Another reference to Kameshwari can be found in the tantric texts of Hinduism, particularly in the Kalika Purana. In this text, she is described as the manifestation of Goddess Parvati, the wife of Lord Shiva, and the goddess of desire and love. She is also considered to be the source of all creativity and inspiration.

modern_usage.modern_context: Kameshwari, also known as Parvati or Shakti, is a popular Hindu goddess worshipped for fertility, love, and prosperity. Her modern depictions can be seen on various digital platforms such as Instagram, Facebook, and Pinterest. On Instagram, Kameshwari is often portrayed through stunning visuals of temples, idols, and spiritual quotes with the hashtag #Kameshwari. On Facebook, groups dedicated to the goddess exist where devotees share experiences, stories, and blessings. Pinterest boards are filled with images of Kameshwari, depicting her in various forms, along with inspirational quotes and meditation techniques related to her. The modern context of Kameshwari's presence on these platforms reflects the trend of incorporating spirituality into daily life through visual representations, social connections, and personal practice.
